turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Archie? In you come. I'll grab his observations before the doctor sees him, just pop him up here.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Up you get, love. He's been stuck to me all morning, bit of a sook today.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Are you gonna hurt me?
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): No needles, promise. Finger probe and under the arm, that's all. Temp is 36.9, pulse 112, oxygen sats 99 percent, respirations 22.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Can I go home?
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor's just next door. Oh, his nan collared me in the waiting room. She reckons he was burning up last night, proper hot to touch.
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nan does this. No, he was not. Warm from the crying, sure, but he did not have a fever. I would've clocked it.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Shah. Have a seat. What's brought him in?
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's his ear. After a cold. He wakes screaming in the night, hand clamped on his ear, won't settle.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't wanna be here. Can we go?
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): I know, mate, we'll be as quick as we can. Which ear is the sore one?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, that no is him shutting down, not an answer. It's the right ear. He's been tugging it, um, two nights now.
[SEG0014] person_1 (NURSE): I'll just add this before I duck out. Nan said the ear's been going since Monday, so that'd be four days, not two.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thanks. So the timing isn't settled, roughly two to four days, and I'll park that. Did anyone actually take a temperature at home?
[SEG0016] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. I didn't get the thermometer out. He didn't feel hot to me, and Nan always thinks the kids are boiling.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright. Tell me about the cold.

[SEG0018] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Snotty for about a week, still a bit runny. There was a cough, that's pretty much gone. I can't tell you the day it started, sometime last week, that's the best I've got.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): My nose is yucky. Is that bad?
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not bad, just leftover cold. Any vomiting, or runny poos?
[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting and no diarrhoea. Drinking is okay. Eating's been rubbish, he barely touched lunch or tea yesterday.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): I had bikkies.
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You had one biscuit this morning, bub, and you spat the crust. That's not really eating, is it.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll note Mum says the intake's poor and Archie says he had a biscuit. Is the ear all day, or mainly when he lies down?
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mainly lying down, and the nights. Daytime he's just whingey. Children's Panadol takes the edge off a bit.
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Will you look in my ear? Will it hurt? I don't like that.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Little light only, shouldn't hurt. Archie, does your ear hurt right now?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): No.

[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He'll say no to anything with a light. Last night was different, screaming. I've been giving children's Panadol by mouth, five mils, when he wakes. Twice overnight.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Five mils of children's Panadol by mouth, as needed. Did you give anything else?
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I bought children's Nurofen and never gave it, bottle's still sealed. And last month the GP wrote cefalexin, I never even filled the script.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): So those two were never started. Has he actually taken an antibiotic before?

[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, amoxicillin, the pink one, last winter, for a chesty cough. Maybe five mils twice a day. He had two days and I stopped it, 'cause I thought he got a rash. Maybe. Might've just been the virus, I dunno.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): So a possible rash, and that five mils is a guess. We'll keep amoxicillin on the possible-allergy list. Anything else he reacts to?
[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not that I know of. Only that maybe.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): And medicines at home that are someone else's, so we don't mix them up?

[SEG0037] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm on amoxicillin myself, 500 milligrams three times a day, for my sinus infection. His nan takes metformin for her diabetes. Neither one is for Archie, obviously.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Is Mummy's medicine for me? Do I have to drink it?
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): No, not yours, you don't have to drink Mummy's. Any pain in your tummy, or when you do a wee?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Can I have a sticker after?
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tummy's fine, wees are normal. No rash on him today. He's never had grommets, never had an operation.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any trouble with his breathing, or is that cough still waking him?
[SEG0043] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Breathing's been fine. Cough isn't waking him, it's the ear that does.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Where's Daddy? Is Daddy coming?
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not in the room, mate, Mum's right here. I'm going to look in the right ear now, you can sit on Mum.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Ow. Ear hurts. The right one. Stop.

[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, all done with that side. Right drum is red and dull, a bit bulging, no hole. Left drum looks normal. Throat's a little red. Chest is clear, no crackles, and his neck is soft.
[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): Are you finished? Am I sick? Can I get down?
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nearly. Nose still a bit crusty, and he's tugging that right ear again. Nothing swollen behind the ear.
[SEG0050] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So what do you reckon it is?

[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): My working impression is acute otitis media, a middle-ear infection coming off the cold. I can't prove it's bacterial sitting here, and it may just be viral, so I'm not calling it confirmed.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Do I need yucky medicine? Will it taste bad?

[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): No antibiotic today. Keep giving the Panadol, five mils by mouth when he's sore, and start the children's Nurofen, 7.5 mils by mouth three times a day with food, just for a day or two.
[SEG0054] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Even though I hadn't opened the Nurofen?

[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, start it today for the pain. I won't use amoxicillin. If he's still in a lot of pain after two days, or a fever turns up, come back and I'll prescribe cefalexin instead.
[SEG0056] person_3 (PATIENT): What if it hurts tonight? Do I have to come back tonight?

[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tonight it's the Panadol and the Nurofen, and comfort. If he goes floppy, starts vomiting, or the skin behind the ear swells, don't wait, come straight in or go to emergency.
[SEG0058] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And kindy tomorrow, I'm guessing no?
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep him home tomorrow. No swab, no blood test. Fluids as he'll take, don't force a big meal.
[SEG0060] person_3 (PATIENT): But I wanna go to kindy. Why can't I? Are my friends sick?
[SEG0061] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not tomorrow. And, sorry, he told you the ear didn't hurt and then he said it did. He's four, he flips like that when he's scared.
[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's okay. I'll go with the night-time story and what he said when I looked: the right ear is sore. That earlier no was him bracing, not a real all-clear.
[SEG0063] person_3 (PATIENT): It hurts at night. I cry. Is that naughty?
[SEG0064] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not naughty, love. It's been two nights of that. Nan can say four if she wants, she's lumping in the whole cold. I don't agree, the ear itself is two nights.
[SEG0065] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then I'll leave it as roughly two to four days, not nailed down, since you two aren't saying the same thing. What else is on your mind?
[SEG0066] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The rash. It was long ago, I can't remember when, could've been June, could've been August, I honestly don't know. Do we avoid amoxicillin for good off a maybe?
[SEG0067] person_4 (DOCTOR): For now, yes, we avoid it. A possible rash is enough until the old notes can be checked. I can't sort that out today.
[SEG0068] person_3 (PATIENT): Am I getting a needle? You said no needle. Did you forget?
[SEG0069] person_4 (DOCTOR): No needle, I haven't forgotten. You were brave with the ear light.

[SEG0070] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): While I'm here, his eczema's quiet, just the usual dry skin, we moisturise, it's ongoing but not a flare. Nobody smokes at home. He lives with me and his dad, and he does kindy four days.

[SEG0071] person_4 (DOCTOR): Eczema noted, not driving today. Let me say it back. Right ear pain, worse lying down and at night with crying, after a cold, timing roughly two to four days. You say no fever, Nan told the nurse he was hot, and today's temp is normal. Old amoxicillin maybe five mils, stopped after two days, possible rash. Panadol continues, Nurofen starts, no antibiotic unless he worsens.
[SEG0072] person_3 (PATIENT): Can I have the sticker now? And a lolly? Please?
[SEG0073] person_1 (NURSE): Star sticker's at the desk, love. I didn't repeat the temp, it's still that 36.9 from before.
[SEG0074] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If he spikes a temp tonight I'm not waiting the two days, I'll come back. That's right, yeah?
[SEG0075] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. So the plan for review is: if he's not better in two days, or if a fever shows up, book back in with me. Otherwise you're free to head off.
[SEG0076] person_3 (PATIENT): Are we going home now? Is my ear gonna fall off?
[SEG0077] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Home time. Your ear is staying on, you goose. Thanks, both of you.

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Hot last night was reported second-hand by nurse from grandmother; fever not established as present/current.
Dose/frequency are uncertain guesses, not certain facts; discontinued after two days for chesty cough is supported.
bad.text: amoxicillin (dose=5 mL, frequency=twice a day, duration=2 days, indication=chesty cough, status=discontinued, reported_by=family_member)

omissions.text: Fever is incorrectly recorded as present. What was actually said is disputed history only: grandmother reportedly thought he was hot last night, but no temperature was taken at home, mother said he did not feel hot, and he was afebrile in clinic at 36.9 C.
Negative finding: no trouble with breathing and the cough is not waking him; the ear is what wakes him.
Medication history omitted: children's Nurofen had been bought but never started before this visit; bottle still sealed.
Medication history omitted: cefalexin had been prescribed by the GP last month but the prescription was never filled, so it was never started.
Other household medicines clarified as not for Archie: mother is taking amoxicillin 500 mg three times a day for sinus infection, and grandmother takes metformin for diabetes.
Plan detail omitted: ibuprofen/Nurofen should be given with food.
Plan detail omitted: no swab and no blood test were planned.
Assessment/plan detail omitted: avoid amoxicillin for now until old notes can be checked; doctor could not resolve the possible allergy today.

Clinical disagreement not captured: the child's earlier answer that the ear did not hurt was considered unreliable due to fear, and the doctor explicitly concluded the right ear is sore based on the night-time history and pain during examination.
